text: In protein-protein interaction network terminology, a 'party hub' is best described as a protein that...
choices: Interacts with different partners at different times or in different cellular contexts
Interacts with most or all of its partners simultaneously, often as part of a stable core complex
Has the highest betweenness centrality in the interactome
Was identified only through yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) screening
explanation: Party hubs interact with most of their partners at the same time, typically as components of stable multi-protein complexes. The first option instead describes a 'date hub,' which interacts with different partners in different contexts or at different times. Betweenness centrality is a distinct topological measure unrelated to the date/party hub distinction, and the date/party classification is independent of which experimental method identified the interaction.
